name: timeline-scrollbar
summary: The temporal NAVIGATOR bar — batch (« ») and single-step (‹ ›) controls around a START–END time WINDOW of bucketed snapshots. Left: batch-back + step-back + the window start; right: the window end + step-forward + batch-forward. Data/behaviour-agnostic: it renders the controls + times and emits `shift {direction, batch}`; the consumer moves its data window. Part of the Playback & Timeline family. Source-derived from netroute/timeline-scrollbar.vue. Reuses obs-button (the step/batch controls, whose obs-icon chevrons inherit --page-text-color so they read dark in light theme / light in dark) + obs-icon.
selectHint: A stepper to move a TIME WINDOW back/forward over bucketed snapshots (netroute history / a temporal chart)? -> obs-timeline-scrollbar. To PICK an absolute date/range -> obs-date-time-picker. To rotate DASHBOARDS -> obs-noc-player.
whenToUse: Under a temporal chart/table whose data is bucketed into fixed windows — the user steps the visible window backward/forward one point or one whole batch at a time.
insteadOf: a hand-built pair of prev/next buttons around two timestamps
a date picker (that selects an absolute point/range; this steps a relative window)
a full scrubber/slider (this is the discrete stepped navigator)

variants.name: default
variants.what: batch-back + step-back + START … END + step-forward + batch-forward.

variants.name: disabled
variants.what: all controls inert (opacity 0.5) — loading, or at the edge of the available range.

sizes.name: default
sizes.note: a full-width strip with a --border-color top rule; step buttons are ~25px tall neutral-lightest; the double-chevron batch buttons are wider.

states.name: rest
states.what: controls neutral-lightest; the two window times between them.

states.name: disabled
states.what: all controls at opacity 0.5, cursor not-allowed; clicks emit nothing.

disabled.note: disable all step/batch controls (loading, or at the edge of the range).

events.name: shift
events.note: a control was clicked; `batch` true = the double-chevron (move a whole window), false = single step (one point). The consumer moves its data window.

decisionFlow: Step a bucketed TIME WINDOW back/forward under a temporal chart/table? -> obs-timeline-scrollbar.
Pick an absolute date or a relative preset range? -> obs-date-time-picker, NOT this.
Rotate through DASHBOARDS on a countdown (wallboard)? -> obs-noc-player.
Single point vs whole window? -> the single chevron emits batch:false (one point); the double chevron emits batch:true (a whole window).

default.useWhen: the data is bucketed into fixed windows and the user steps the visible window backward/forward
default.dontUse: for absolute date/range selection (that is obs-date-time-picker)
default.example: under the netroute history chart: « ‹  Jul 21 06:00 PM … 06:15 PM  › »

disabled.useWhen: data is loading, or the window is already at the earliest/latest available bucket
disabled.dontUse: as a permanent read-only display — if it never steps, it should not be shown
disabled.example: disabled while the history query is in flight

usage.note: One per temporal chart context (netroute history). The product wires it to a chart context that shifts the window; the DS element emits `shift` for the consumer to handle.

do: Place it directly under the temporal chart/table it scrubs (the top rule reads as the divider).
Wire `shift` to move your data window (single point vs whole batch via the `batch` flag).
Show the current window's start/end in `start`/`end`.
Disable it while loading or at the range boundary.
dont: Don't use it to select an absolute date/range — that's obs-date-time-picker.
Don't use it to rotate dashboards — that's obs-noc-player.

a11y.summary: Each step/batch control REUSES obs-button (keyboard-operable) with an aria-label/title (Previous window / Step back / Step forward / Next window); the chevron icons are decorative. Disabled buttons carry the disabled attribute. Announce the new window's start/end via an aria-live region so keyboard/screen-reader users hear where they moved.
a11y.notes: The step vs batch distinction is only visual (single vs double chevron) — the aria-labels carry it (Step back vs Previous window). Announce the resulting window range on shift. Keep the buttons keyboard-reachable (they are native buttons).

knownIssues: The bar is a discrete STEPPER, not a draggable slider — the product's timeline-scrollbar.vue also only exposes step/batch controls (a draggable handle was scaffolded but commented out). Times are formatted by the consumer and passed in as `start`/`end` strings.
